text:
Will Cuylle has 82 hits in 21 games, and that's the part of his game that never slumps. The scoring has. He hasn't scored in eight games on 2.9 expected goals and hasn't had a point in five, and a short experiment at centre has reportedly already ended.

The chances say this will turn. He has 4 goals on 7.6 expected, and his own shot quality, 1.32 expected goals per 60, is the best of his career and above last season's 1.00. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him taking 2.2 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net, the best kind of looks. Those go in. The Rangers have also scored 4.8 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice.

The honest caveat is the rest of his game this season. The Rangers take 52% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, a bit below their team rate, and our model notes chances against pile up with him on. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him in the 94th percentile for taking chances away, so that's probably noise too. Our talent range still projects about 20 goals. A player getting this many good looks rarely stays stuck.
